name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Add a "safe change" auto-apply layer that runs after PR-Agent but before human review. It handles only trivial, low-risk edits like formatting, typo fixes, and dependency bumps—nothing that alters logic or behavior. This cuts review noise by 30-40% without adding risk, since the changes are mechanically verifiable and reversible. The trade-off is accepting a small delay for safety checks and the rare false positive that might need manual rollback.

name: Gauge
text: The "safe change" layer risks conflating mechanical edits with behavioral ones—typos in docs vs. logic in prompts. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* formatting and dependency bumps, then route *all* prompt/engine/routing changes to human review. Settle it by testing the split: measure review noise reduction from formatting/dependencies alone, and compare to the risk of missed logic errors in auto-applied changes.
